verdict.rationale: Anytime Mailbox's own docs say it provides a real street address rather than a P.O. Box, and that this address meets business registration requirements in most states, which covers the LLC-registration part. The evidence never mentions acceptance by banks for KYC, and vendor-form use is only implied by general business-address testimonials. The registration claim is also qualified to 'most states'. Missing for 10: evidence of bank KYC acceptance, explicit vendor-form acceptance, all-state registration coverage, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, I get a real street address (not a PO Box) that works for LLC registration, bank KYC, and vendor forms

citations.quote: A virtual mailbox provides a real street address that meets business registration requirements in most states.
It provides you with a real street address, where your mail is received, scanned, and uploaded to your account.
I purchased a mailbox to establish a business address for my home-based web design company.
